en: Around Xi'an: One Place, One Full Day
zh: 西安周边：一天只选一处

p.src: A regional map makes Lintong, Huashan, Han Yangling, Cuihuashan and Qianling look like a tidy ring around Xi'an. A day, however, is governed less by straight-line distance than by its logistics: when you leave the hotel, how many transfers remain outside the city, how far you walk on site, and when the return must begin. Choose one place according to what you want to understand. Combining sites simply because they lie in the same direction often turns the most important visit into a rushed glance.

p.src: The connectors show direction, not a railway, road or live navigation route. A day in Lintong, east of Xi'an, is organised around archaeology. Farther east, Huashan works only when the train, local transfer and mountain transport are planned as one chain. Han Yangling to the north is easiest with a prearranged car; Cuihuashan to the south is a managed mountain day; Qianling to the west still requires a transfer from Qianxian. Count the stages of the journey before judging distance on the map.

caption.zh: 西安周边五种单日选择。虚线只示方向；下方交通链用于比较换乘环节，不是铁路、公路、时间或实时导航。
caption.ja: 西安近郊の五つの日帰り候補。破線は方角のみを示し、下の移動段階は乗り継ぎを比べるためのもの。鉄道、道路、所要時間、当日のナビではない。
caption.en: Five one-day choices around Xi'an. Dashed joins show direction only; the transport chains compare stages rather than depict railways, roads, journey times or live navigation.

p.src: Choose Lintong to understand how military formations, subsidiary pits and the central mound formed one Qin funerary landscape. Choose Huashan if you want a genuine mountain walk and accept that weather may change the plan. Choose Han Yangling for a quieter encounter with Western Han burial pits, small human figures and animal models. Choose Cuihuashan to read a landslide landscape through rock seas, caves in collapse debris and dammed lakes. Choose Qianling to study Tang imperial burial through its spirit way, stone sculpture and associated tombs. Skip mountain outings in doubtful weather; skip Han Yangling or Qianling unless the final transfer and return are arranged.

p.src: Make the Qin Shi Huang Mausoleum Museum the core of a Lintong day. Its two visitor areas serve different purposes: the Terracotta Army Museum presents Pits 1, 2 and 3 and related displays, while Lishan Garden reconnects the burial mound and subsidiary pits to the wider mausoleum. Enter within your real-name reservation slot, give each area enough uninterrupted time, and allow for the museum shuttle and queues. If you start late, meet heavy crowds or spend longer at the pits, drop Huaqing Palace rather than rush Lishan Garden.

p.src: Huaqing Palace is not a footnote to the Qin mausoleum; it offers a different timeline. The Imperial Bathing Pool Site Museum presents excavated remains of Tang royal bathing pools, while the Five-Room Hall is a historic site connected with the 1936 Xi'an Incident. The present gardens, archaeological remains, later buildings and modern visitor facilities cannot be treated as an intact Tang palace. Metro Line 9 reaches Huaqingchi station. If you add Huaqing after the Qin museum, decide whether the bathing pools or modern history is your focus; do not also force Mount Li and the night performance into the day.

p.src: Choose your route on the mountain before buying the tickets for it. Huashan North station is only the first stage; you still need a local transfer to the visitor centre, a scenic bus, a cableway and walks between peaks. A West Peak cableway round trip keeps most of the walking among the higher peaks. Going up by West Peak and down by North Peak shows more of the ridge but leaves a long walk between the two. A North Peak cableway round trip still involves substantial ascent if you continue to the higher peaks. On a first visit, do not try to cover all five. Mark where you will go up, come down and turn back on the official route map, then verify both trains on China Railway 12306.

p.src: A Huashan day needs four firm conditions: a confirmed reservation, official notice that the intended entrance and cableway are operating, weather and visibility suitable for exposed sections, and a generous return margin. Check once the night before and again before leaving. Wear shoes with reliable grip, keep both hands free for rails and steps, and carry water plus an adjustable wind-and-rain layer. Work backwards from the train through descent, queues, scenic bus and station transfer; do not aim for the last service. Shorten the route or return another day if winds strengthen, visibility deteriorates, cableway operations change or you feel unwell.

p.src: Han Yangling is for close archaeological observation rather than spectacle. Begin in the archaeological exhibition hall to understand Emperor Jing, Empress Wang and the mausoleum plan, then enter the external-pit protection hall. Glass walkways pass above and beside ten external pits, keeping the remains and visitors in separate, controlled environments. Small human figures, animal models and domestic objects show how Han court roles and routines were classified and represented within the funerary landscape; this is not a miniature Terracotta Army. The entrance is on the airport expressway, so arrange the outbound and return rides, including the exact pickup point, before leaving. Although the airport looks close on the map, do not fit this visit into a tight pre-flight margin.

p.src: Visit Cuihuashan as a geological field site, not as a hunt for one viewpoint. Landslide scarps, rock seas, caves formed within collapse debris and dammed lakes belong to one collapse landscape. Read the interpretation first, then use open paths to compare the direction of blocks, deposits at the foot of slopes and the position of water. A scenic-area ticket is not permission to continue into the Qinling interior. Xi'an's current notice prohibits unauthorized crossings, exploration, climbing and camping in the core protection zone, as well as leaving developed scenic areas for those activities. After rain, in icy conditions or extreme heat, and whenever a route is closed, stay on managed paths or cancel the mountain day.

p.src: At Qianling, begin with the southern approach and spirit way of the main mausoleum. Along one axis, gate-tower remains, winged horses, ostrich reliefs, stone figures, the Shusheng Ji Stele and the Wordless Stele bring together the mountain setting, ceremonial assembly and imperial burial practice. The main chamber has not been excavated; read the evidence above ground instead of filling the unopened chamber with treasure stories. In the afternoon, choose one associated tomb or museum confirmed open that day. Its murals, figures and chamber plan provide a second body of evidence. Official directions describe either Qianxian station followed by local bus or taxi, or travel by road throughout. Confirm both the opening status and return transport before leaving. As of this book's August 2026 fact check, the official site still carried a conservation notice for the passage to the Yongtai Princess Tomb. Check current access and do not build the entire day around one underground site.

p.src: A cableway removes part of the ascent; it does not level the mountain. Even at the upper station, long flights of stone steps, narrow sections, railings, wind and sudden cloud remain. Keep the pack light, water within reach and watch the surface underfoot. For a photograph, stop on a secure, wide spot without blocking the path. The four guides stop on a managed section because the day's final objective is a safe return, not one more peak.

caption.zh: 索道之后仍要走山路。四位向导在有护栏的宽处停下，查看路面、风势和返程余量。这里示意有管理的山地步道，不对应华山某一峰段。
caption.ja: ロープウェーの先にも山道が続く。四人は手すりのある広い場所で、路面、風、帰路の余裕を確かめる。管理された山道の例で、華山の特定区間ではない。
caption.en: A cableway does not end the mountain walk. The four guides pause on a broad, railed landing to check the surface, wind and return margin. This is a managed path, not a specific Huashan section.

p.src: Check only six things the night before: confirmed reservation, matching booking and identity-document details, weather and official notice, every outbound stage, every return stage, and the latest turn-around time. Check again in the morning. In Lintong, reserve enough time for both Qin museum areas. At Huashan and Cuihuashan, put weather limits and open boundaries first. At Han Yangling and Qianling, arrange the return ride first. If any condition fails, remove the optional stop and then shorten the core route; change destination only if the plan still does not work. If weather cancels a mountain day, switch to Han Yangling or one city museum. Do not improvise on an unmanaged mountain path.
